newsitem.title: JAPAN: Securities houses' shares hurt by gloomy forecast.
newsitem.headline: Securities houses' shares hurt by gloomy forecast.

text.p: Shares of securities houses slipped across the board in Friday morning trade, dragged down by a string of announcements by the firms on Thursday that they expect losses in the first half of the current business year, traders said.
The securities sector was the largest percentage loser in the first section of the Tokyo Stock Exchange as of 0149 GMT.
Seven second-tier Japanese brokerages said on Thursday they would post losses in the first half of the current business year, hurt by lower-than-expected stock turnover and falling market share.

The parent current losses at the seven firms are expected to range from Dai-Ichi Securities' 800 million yen to Kankaku Securities' 4.1 billion yen for the first six months. The other five are New Japan Securities, Wako Securities, Yamatane Securities, Cosmo Securities and Tokyo Securities

The country's biggest securities house, Nomura Securities Co Ltd, also said separately that it would post net losses in the six months to September 30 as it provides financial support to a non-bank affiliate.
